name: CICO Media – Image Usage, Media Tags & Real Proportions
author: digimatica

sections.description:
CICO Media improves the native WordPress Media Library instead of replacing it with another media manager. You keep the Library you know and gain the answers it never gave: is this image used, where, and how do I find it again.

Find unused images and see where each image is used

Every card shows Used · N or No usage. Open the Where used panel to see the pages and posts that use the image, with a link to edit each one. A filter shows only the images with no usage found, so you know where to start when you clean up. CICO Media reads post content, Gutenberg blocks, featured images, the site icon and the logo, and keeps its index up to date in the background without slowing your site.

Organize your media with tags, not folders

Create tags such as “Products”, “Team” or “Blog” and add them to an image from its details panel. Files never move and URLs never change, so nothing breaks. One image can have several tags, which folders cannot do. You can filter by tag in the Media Library and in the Media Picker.

Find the right image while you edit a page

The usage and tag filters also work in the Media Picker, the window you open for a featured image or an image block. Filter by tag and pick the right image without scrolling through hundreds of files.

See the real proportions and the aspect ratio

Portrait, landscape and square images show in their real proportions, with no square crop. The aspect ratio (16:9, 4:3, 1:1…) is printed on every card, so you know right away whether an image fits a banner, a cover or a thumbnail.

Details on every card

  • Dimensions, file size, file type and file name, with clean truncation for long names.
  • Quick Info: a larger preview and the main details without leaving the Library.
  • The same cards in the Media Picker used by posts, pages and compatible builders.
  • Adjustable card sizes.

What CICO Media does not do

It does not delete, move, compress or modify your files, and it is not a folder manager. “No usage” means that no reference was found in the sources it reads, not that a file is safe to delete: keep a backup before you delete media.

Go deeper with CICO Media Pro

CICO Media Pro is an optional extension. It reads usage in Elementor, WPBakery, WooCommerce, Advanced Custom Fields and theme settings, with the exact field or element and a Live / Not live / Unknown status. It adds bulk tagging and the CICO Filters bar, which combines usage, status, tag, orientation, file size, file type and source. You can try it free for 14 days, with no credit card. Learn more at https://cicomediawp.com.

External services

CICO Media works without contacting any external service. It does not track you or send usage data.

Two features are optional and only run when you use them:

  • Licensing for CICO Media Pro (Freemius). If you choose to activate a CICO Media Pro license, the bundled Freemius SDK connects to Freemius (https://freemius.com) to validate the license. It sends your license key, your site URL, the WordPress and PHP versions and the email address you confirm. Nothing is sent unless you start the activation. The “Try Pro free for 14 days” button only opens the Freemius checkout in a new tab; nothing is sent until you submit the form there. Terms: https://freemius.com/terms/ Privacy policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/
  • Send feedback. The feedback form in the plugin settings sends the message and optional attachments you write to the CICO Media developers by email through your site’s mail system (wp_mail). It runs only when you press send.
sections.installation:
1. Install CICO Media from WordPress or upload the plugin ZIP.
  2. Activate CICO Media.
  3. Open Media > Library in Grid view.
  4. Configure optional enhancements under Media > CICO Media.
sections.faq:
Does CICO Media replace the WordPress Media Library?

No. It improves the native Media Library and the native Media Picker. Your media, folders, URLs and workflow stay exactly as WordPress provides them.

Does it change, move, compress or delete my files?

No. CICO Media never modifies media files or attachment URLs. It only changes how media is presented and adds read-only details.

Does it work in the media picker of the block editor and page builders?

Yes. It enhances the native WordPress media picker (featured image, “Add media”, and builders that use it) with the same cards, without adding requests when the picker opens.

Do I need CICO Media Pro?

No. CICO Media works on its own, including usage, tags and the two toolbar filters. CICO Media Pro is an optional extension that reads more sources (Elementor, WPBakery, WooCommerce, ACF, theme settings), adds the Live / Not live status, bulk tagging and combined filters. You can find out more at https://cicomediawp.com.

Which usage does CICO Media find?

Images used in post and page content, in blocks (including nested blocks), as featured image, and as site icon and logo. An image that is used only in a page builder, a custom field or a shop shows as “No usage” in the free plugin. The Usage screen lists the sources that are active on your site and not read.

Can I trust “No usage” to delete an image?

Use it as a starting point, not as a guarantee. Images can be used by custom code, builders or fields that CICO Media does not read. Keep a backup and delete in small batches.

How do I find unused images in WordPress?

Open Media > Library in Grid view and use the usage filter to show only the images with “No usage found”. Open the Where used panel on any image to check it before you decide. “No usage” is a starting point: keep a backup and delete in small batches.

How can I organize the Media Library without folders?

Use Media Tags. Create a tag, add it to an image from its details panel, and filter the Library or the Media Picker by tag. Files and URLs never move, and one image can have several tags.

How can I see which page uses an image?

Click the Used badge on a card, or open the image details, to see the Where used panel with the pages and posts that use it and a link to edit each one.

Can I tag many images at once?

In the free plugin you tag one image at a time. Bulk tagging, selecting many images and adding or removing tags in one step, is part of CICO Media Pro.

Does it find images used in WooCommerce products?

The free plugin does not read WooCommerce product galleries and variations: an image used only there shows as “No usage”. CICO Media Pro reads them, and also Elementor, WPBakery and ACF.

Where are the settings?

Under Media > CICO Media. You can choose which details appear on the cards and the card size.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

Deactivating keeps your settings. Deleting the plugin removes its options and its usage index. Media Tags are kept unless you choose to delete them in the settings. Your media library is never touched.

Which versions of WordPress and PHP are supported?

WordPress 6.4 or later and PHP 7.4 or later.
sections.changelog:
1.1.3

  • The Italian translation is now included in the plugin, so it works right away on Italian sites.

1.1.2

  • Translation: the usage, Where used, tags and index-status texts added in 1.1 are now fully translatable, including the “pending” counter. Italian translation updated for all of them.

1.1.1

  • Settings: the option to delete Media Tags on uninstall is now shown without Pro and applies when CICO Media is deleted.

1.1.0

  • Usage is now part of the free plugin: Used / No usage on every card, a Where used panel for post content, blocks and featured images, and a background usage index.
  • Media Tags are now free: create tags, add them to an image, see them on the cards.
  • Two toolbar filters in the Media Library and the Media Picker: usage and tag.
  • Fix: the usage index no longer reads its queue before its tables exist on first activation.
  • Deleting the plugin now also removes the usage index; Media Tags are kept unless you choose to delete them.
  • CICO Media Pro 1.1 extends these features. If CICO Media Pro older than 1.1 is active, update it.

1.0.1

  • New 14-day free trial of CICO Media Pro, with no credit card. Start it from the Pro section of the plugin Overview.

1.0.0

  • Initial public release.
  • Real image proportions, dimensions, aspect ratio and filename on every card in the native Media Library.
  • Quick Info and attachment-details enhancements.
  • Enhanced native Media Picker with no extra requests when it opens.
  • Adjustable card sizes and per-detail display settings.
